text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-db-prod (db-conn-saturation). Pager: pagerduty. Severity: P1. Links: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-12345

pagerduty: Incident INC-12345 created and escalated to eng-oncall. First responder: kevin.

kevin: I got the page, looking now.

mike: ack — on my way. grabbing logs and pg stats.

kevin: quick context — we started seeing slow write latencies ~18:23 UTC and a spike in application errors timeouts to DB. Affects ingestion and user-facing writes. Reads mostly ok.

sara: seeing a lot of `connection_pool_exhausted` in prod-app logs and 503s from /submit endpoints.

mike: running `psql -h redwood-db-prod -c "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity;"` now.

kevin: paste results when you have them. also check `max_connections` and `waiting` state.

mike: output:
```
 count 
-------
  510
(1 row)
```

mike: pg max_connections is 500 on this host. so we are above the limit — processes are queueing.

kevin: that matches app errors. which pool is leaking? tagging @julia for recent deploys.

julia: I rolled the ingestion service ~17:50 UTC with a config bump to pool_size=20 for nginx-worker. Haven't changed DB pool config. Might be a burst from a backfill job.

sara: metrics: p95 write latency jumped from 120ms -> 3.2s at 18:20. connection_queued_count increased sharply.

opsbot: CPU on db host db-prod-1 is normal (55%). No OOM. Disk and network nominal.

kevin: immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle ingestion backfill job, 2) temporary increase max_connections (requires restart), 3) bounce app pools to release leaked connections, 4) fail over to reader (not ideal for writes). Thoughts?

mike: we can throttle the backfill via k8s job controller — I can scale it down to 0 replicas.

kevin: do that as first action. mike, scale down and confirm.

mike: `kubectl scale job ingestion-backfill --replicas=0 -n prod` -> done. job scaled to 0.

sara: seeing tail off in new connection rate already. inbound conn/sec down 70% since command.

kevin: good. but we still have >500 active sessions. need to reduce. Could we gracefully recycle app worker pools to free idle connections? That avoids DB restart.

julia: yes we can rotate deployment with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/api-ingest -n prod --timeout=5m`. That will restart pods one at a time. Doable.

kevin: do one pod at a time to avoid full outage. mike, coordinate with traffic router. Set maxUnavailable: 1.

mike: starting rollout. command executed. watching.

opsbot: pod api-ingest-3 restarted (18:42:10 UTC).

sara: connections dropped ~40 when that pod restarted. p95 latency down to 850ms. Partial recovery.

kevin: continue rolling. keep an eye on error rate. if errors spike, pause.

julia: rolling next pod now.

mike: after 3/5 pods restarted, active connections at 260. still > capacity headroom but improving.

sara: customer impact: payments ingestion backlog delayed ~3-6 min for ~12% of customers. External API timeouts observed at 18:27-18:45. Logged as degraded.

kevin: updating PD incident with customer impact: degraded writes for ~12% users, partial backlog growth.

pagerduty: Incident INC-12345 updated: status=acknowledged by kevin.

opsbot: DB replication lag normal. No replica promotion needed.

mike: connections now 190, p95 latency 220ms, errors trending down.

kevin: good. keep rolling until all pods restarted and active connections < 120. then we can consider closing incident or moving to monitoring.

julia: final pod restarted. active connections 98. p95 110ms. errors returned to baseline.

sara: verified ingestion throughput normal. backlog processing resumed.

kevin: I'll perform a quick postmortem checklist: root cause hypothesis = concurrent backfill job + slightly low app connection pool sizing leading to pool exhaustion and hitting Postgres max_connections.

mike: mitigation timeline: 18:38 scale down backfill, 18:42 start app rollout, 18:56 all pods rotated, 19:00 connections below threshold.

julia: actions: 1) block backfill scheduling until we have dynamic throttle in place, 2) increase pg max_connections to 600 on next maintenance window and add monitoring alert before approaching 80% usage, 3) add app-level circuit-breaker to limit aggressive retry/backfill concurrency.

kevin: agreed. I'll create a follow-up ticket with these action items and assign owners. Also suggest adding an automated PD escalation to DB-owners if connections > 80% for >5m.

pagerduty: Incident INC-12345 status changed to resolved by kevin. Resolution note: scaled down backfill and rotated app pods to free connections; monitoring in place.

kevin: handing off to julia for post-incident follow-up and any customer comms. @julia take it from here.

julia: taking handoff. scheduling follow-up review. tagging product for customer comms.

sara: adding log snippet for root-cause timeline to the ticket: `2026-03-14T18:20:12Z ERROR pool-exhausted conn_wait=12`

mike: thanks team. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
